Nothing gives us more sincere pleasure than
to note the material progress of our country;
and we are very sure that our public-spirited
fellow citizens every where will rejoice to
learn the facts going to show the unusual
progress of the region tributary to the great
work Of this section of the confederacy, the
Baltimore and Ohio Railroad, embraced in the
following extract from the Baltimore Sun OF
Saturday last:


FREIGHT FROM THE WKsT-The freiehtinp
business of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad

cedently large. The companys receipts for
october and November amounted to more thar
one hundred thousand dollars in excess Of last
year for the same period Judging from the
immense trade now passing upon the road,
and from the heavy contracts which we learn
have been made by its active western agents
for the season, the revenue must show a still
greater increase for this and the ensuing win
ter months.


From the lst to the 10th instant, as We are
credibly informed, the large number Of one
hundred car loads, eight wheeled, double }
containing some eight hundred and fifty tons,
have been the daily average Of produce dis
patched from Wheeling for Baltimore and the
more eastern markets, especially Of New York
and Boston. From the 10th to the 10th in
slant, inclusive, this vast quantity has been
increased to the average of fully one thous sand
tons per day, and during the first four days of
TIC present week the enormous amount of four
thousand Elk hundred tons has been loaded
and dispatched eastwardly from the Wheeling
station, being al average of nearly twelve
hundred tons per day.


Besides this immense trade in -four pork,
&c, the live stock ansportation has been
fully maintained This important and grow
Ing feature in the business of the road
has been represented by the arrival since the
lst instant Of from seventeen to twenty thou

TiOr counties Of Virginia


The great rush of trade this season has not

As measure Of relief, the work of archine

The immense warehouse built by the New

nient and appropriate arrangement.

PROPERTIES OF CHARcoAL.-Wood charcoal
possesses highly absorbent power for ammo
niaoal gasses. suphurated hydrogen, suphu-
rous acid, and carbonic acid gas This prop
orty perfectly adapts it to the absorption OF
putrid exhaetions from decaying animal bo-
dies, layer from one to two inches in thick
ness being sufficient entirely to absorb the
efiuvia from large animals. From dead dogs
thus covered no eitiuyia were perceptible, while
the decomposition Ofthe bodies was accelerated.
This arises from the fact that charcoal absorbs
and Oxydizes the efiiuyia which, under
ordinary circumstances, would be evolved d.
rectly into the air; but within the pores of
the charcoal they are brought into contact
with condensed oxygen, and are thus subjected
to species of low combustion, their carbon
being converted into carbonc acid, and their
hydrogen into water. Charcoal, therefore.
instead of being antiseptic, is precisely the
reverse.
